scenes.text: Outside the wall, medieval suburbs began to grow around the Christian Wall of the 12th century.

scenes.caption: Photo 1860
scenes.text: The Puerta del Sol originated as one of the gates in the city wall that surrounded Madrid in the 15th century.

scenes.caption: Photo 1870
scenes.text: The House of the Post Office was built by French architect Jacques Marquet between 1766 and 1768.

scenes.caption: Photo 1880
scenes.text: There are two commemorative plaques in the front of the Royal House of the Post Office: one is devoted to the neighbours of Madrid who rose up against the Napoleonic invasion of Spain on 2 May 1808; the other one is a memorial of…

scenes.caption: Photo 1880
scenes.text: The New Year's celebration has been broadcast live since 31 December 1962 on major radio and television networks including Atresmedia and RTVE.

scenes.caption: Photo 1895
scenes.text: The Puerta del Sol has seen protests against the 2004 Madrid bombings on commuter trains, and Spain's involvement in the Iraq War.

scenes.caption: Photo 1905
scenes.text: Until 2009, the statue stood on the north side at the entrance to Calle del Carmen.

scenes.caption: Photo 1910
scenes.text: In 2011, the square became established as a focal point and a symbol for the ongoing anti-austerity movement in Spain.

scenes.caption: Photo 1920
scenes.text: Despite once being the meeting point of the six major radial roads of Spain, in 2020 the square was pedestrianized and closed to most traffic.

scenes.title: The place
scenes.text: Kilometre zero of Spain's roads, the square was redesigned in 1857-1862. Horse-drawn, then electric trams crossed it at the turn of the century.
